subject: Civil Engineering
title: Traffic Calming: Slowing Cars Down
description: A short lesson to help you apply Traffic Calming: Slowing Cars Down.

hook.text: Neighborhood streets designed like highways invite speeding. The design must change.

buildup.text: Speed bumps force drivers to slow down. Chicanes make drivers weave through offsets.

discovery.text: Narrowing lanes with curb extensions makes drivers feel the road is tighter — they slow.

twist.text: Raised crosswalks prioritize pedestrians and force cars to yield physically.

climax.text: Woonerf streets in the Netherlands share space equally — cars crawl at walking pace.

punchline.text: Design the street for slow speeds and drivers obey without signs.

quiz.question: How does narrowing a lane calm traffic?
options: It blocks larger vehicles from entering the street
Drivers perceive a tighter road and instinctively reduce speed
It increases traffic congestion, forcing everyone to stop

details.summary: Traffic calming uses physical design features like speed humps, chicanes, raised crosswalks, and narrowed lanes to reduce vehicle speeds in residential and commercial areas.
details.whyItMatters: Reducing vehicle speed from 50 to 30 km/h cuts pedestrian fatality risk by approximately 80%. Traffic calming protects vulnerable road users in areas where fast vehicle speeds conflict with community livability.
takeaways: Speed humps reduce average speeds by 10-15 km/h on residential streets
Chicanes and curb extensions narrow the visual field to slow drivers naturally
Raised crosswalks improve pedestrian visibility while acting as speed control

faq.question: What is the difference between a speed hump and a speed bump?
faq.answer: Speed humps are gradual raised areas spanning the full road width, typically 3-4 meters long and 75-100 mm high, designed for 25-30 km/h travel. Speed bumps are shorter and more abrupt, only 0.3-1 meter long, forcing near-stops. Humps are for streets; bumps are for parking lots.

faq.question: Do traffic calming measures cause problems for emergency vehicles?
faq.answer: Some measures like speed humps can delay fire trucks and ambulances by 5-10 seconds each. Modified designs like speed cushions have gaps aligned with wide-axle emergency vehicles. Raised intersections slow all vehicles equally. Emergency service consultation is essential during design.
